standard_prerequisites.use: Gives that f itself is proper, hence f(X) is closed and images of closed points are closed, the starting point of the fibre analysis.

standard_prerequisites.name: Proper morphisms with finite fibres are finite locally on the base
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: More on Morphisms, Lemma more-morphisms-lemma-proper-finite-fibre-finite-in-neighbourhood; Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma coherent-lemma-proper-finite-fibre-finite-in-neighbourhood
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the pointwise finiteness of the closed fibres into finiteness of f over an open neighbourhood of each image point.

core_obligations: Properness (proof lines 335-338): f is proper because X is proper over k and Y is separated over k; hence f(X) is closed and images of closed points are closed.

Fibres over closed points are finite (proof lines 339-345): for y the image of a closed point, the fibre f^{-1}({y}) is a closed subset of X containing no generic point of any dimension-1 irreducible component by hypothesis (3); a closed subset of a scheme of dimension at most 1 avoiding all one-dimensional generic points is a finite set of points.

Local finiteness and conclusion (proof lines 346-352): f is finite over an open neighbourhood of y by the proper-finite-fibre lemma (in the Noetherian case the easier Cohomology of Schemes variant suffices); hypothesis (3) provides enough such closed points y, which completes the proof.
proof_roadmap: Derive properness of f and closedness of f(X) and of point images.
Analyze the fibre over the image of a closed point: closed, avoids all one-dimensional generic points, hence finite.
Apply the proper-plus-finite-fibres lemma to get finiteness over neighbourhoods, and cover by enough image points.
difficulty_reason: The lemma gives a practical finiteness criterion for morphisms from proper dimension-1 schemes (statement lines 322-333). The proof (lines 335-352) is a genuine fibre analysis: properness of f from the separatedness of Y, the dimension bookkeeping that a closed subset of a scheme of dimension at most 1 with no one-dimensional generic points is finite, and the passage from finite closed fibres to local finiteness through the proper-finite-fibre lemma. H2: short, but the dimension bookkeeping and the covering conclusion carry the argument and neither is a citation.
